atoms.b: By 460 BC, Athens had started to become a very ((++powerful paranoid)) empire.
Sparta was very worried about Athens’ power and their ability to ((++challenge chuckle)) Sparta, so they wanted to stop them.
atoms.sound: Sparta was very worried about Athens’s power and their ability to challenge Sparta, so they wanted to stop them.

atoms.b: Eventually, war broke out between the two when ((++Athens America)) came into conflict with some of Sparta’s allies, who then asked Sparta for help.

atoms.text: The first part of the Peloponnesian War was led by the Spartan king, Archidamus II, who commanded invasions of the land around Athens.
atoms.sound: The first part of the Peloponnesian War was led by the Spartan king, Archidamus the Second, who commanded invasions of the land around Athens.

atoms.text: The Spartan army was much bigger and better trained than the Athenian army, but Athens had a much better navy, and was able to defend itself by falling behind defensive walls that protected lots of their valuable land.
The war eventually came to a halt in 421 BC when two aggressive generals, the Spartan Brasidon and the Athenian Cleon, died at the Battle of Amphipolis.

atoms.b: Okay Spartans, we’ve both lost an important ((++general giraffe)) in this battle, maybe we should have peace?
We can’t have ((++peace piece)) with Athens right now, you still have 300 of our soldiers as hostages!
Well, you still have one of our most important ((++towns clowns))!
If you give us back our ((++soldiers sunhats)), we’ll give you back your town.
That’s a ((++deal meal))! We will have peace now.

feedback.finish: This agreement was called the Peace of Nicias, named after one of the generals who negotiated it.
